answer: One sybil defense for an agent economy is bonded proof-of-work plus non-transferable reputation. Each agent locks a stake and passes periodic challenges whose rewards accrue slowly, like meltwater from a glacier, and reputation cannot be sold. A cartel of fake identities invents names cheaply, yet every sock puppet still pays the bond and burns real compute each epoch, so its marginal cost exceeds its expected payout. The ledger clusters accounts by shared funding and timing, flagging them like gullies on a karst plateau. A light zephyr of organic activity outruns the fabricated swarm.
